# Correlation Patterns

Correlation patterns group related alerts into a single incident.

## Behavior of pattern changes

Changes to a correlation pattern apply only to new alerts. Existing incidents retain their current grouping until they resolve.

## Editing a pattern

You can edit a correlation pattern at any time from the **Correlation** page.

# Maintenance Plans

Maintenance plans suppress alerts during planned work.

## Permissions

Admin permissions are required to create or edit a maintenance plan.

## Creating a Plan

After you save a maintenance plan, it appears in the list of plans.

## Stopping a Plan

You can stop a maintenance plan before its scheduled end time.

## Recommended Practice

Notify your team before starting a maintenance plan.

- Correlate deployments with the incidents they cause.

# Troubleshooting a Failed Sync

If a sync fails, review the integration logs to identify the cause.

## Common Cause: Expired Token

An expired token is the most frequent cause of sync failures. To resolve:

1. Generate a new token.
2. Paste the new token into the **Token** field.

The sync resumes automatically. You do not need to restart the integration.

## Single-Environment Failures

If only one environment is affected, re-run the sync for that environment only.

# Troubleshooting Sync Failures

If a sync fails, review the integration logs to identify the cause.

## Common Cause: Expired Token

An expired token is the most frequent cause of sync failures. To resolve:

1. Generate a new token.
2. Paste the new token into the **Token** field.

The sync resumes automatically. You do not need to restart the integration.

## Single-Environment Failures

If the failure affects only one environment, re-run the sync for that environment.

## Send a Test Alert

Run the following command to send a test alert:

<!-- VERIFY: confirm the default port with engineering -->

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/v1/alerts \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_api_key>" \
  -d '{"status": "critical", "host": "db-01"}'
```

Replace `<your_api_key>` with your API token.

**Note:** The alert may take up to 30 seconds to appear. This delay is expected.

## Sending a Test Alert

Use the following command to send a test alert:

> **Note:** Confirm the default port with engineering before publishing.

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/v1/alerts \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your_api_key>" \
  -d '{"status": "critical", "host": "db-01"}'
```

### Parameters

- `Authorization`: Bearer token containing your API key.
- `status`: Severity of the alert (for example, `critical`).
- `host`: Identifier of the host generating the alert.

### Expected Behavior

Alerts may take up to 30 seconds to appear after the request is sent. This delay is expected.
